headline: Dance is universal—every human culture moves rhythmically to express what words cannot
universal_truth: Some truths are embodied, not spoken; the body knows things the mind cannot articulate
fun_facts: Evidence of dance dates back 9,000 years—cave paintings showing people dancing together
Dance activates reward centers in the brain—it's neurologically pleasurable
Mirror neurons fire when watching dance—we internally dance along even while sitting still
discussion_questions: Why do we dance at celebrations?
What can dance express that words cannot?
When did you last dance, and how did it feel?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Every culture on Earth dances. From tribal ceremonies to nightclubs, humans move together to rhythm. We danced before we wrote, before we farmed, maybe before we had language. Dance is as human as speech.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Dance takes energy, can be embarrassing, and serves no obvious survival purpose. Yet every society develops dance. What need does this universal behavior fulfill?

options.text: Dance expresses emotion, builds social bonds, and synchronizes groups in ways language cannot
options.response: Yes. Moving together creates connection. Rhythm synchronizes heartbeats and brain waves. Dance builds community through shared movement.

options.text: Dance evolved for mating displays like in other animals
options.response: Mating plays a role, but dance serves much broader social functions...

q1.title: Synchronizing Groups
q1.script: When people move together in rhythm, their heart rates synchronize. Their brain waves align. Trust increases. Pain tolerance rises. Dance literally puts a group on the same wavelength—it's social bonding through movement.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Synchronizing Groups"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Before Words
q2.script: Dance may predate language. Early humans couldn't explain complex emotions, but they could move together. Dance communicates what words can't capture—grief, joy, longing, celebration. The body speaks first.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Mirror Neurons
q3.script: When you watch someone dance, mirror neurons fire as if you're dancing too. You internally rehearse their movements. That's why watching dance feels engaging—your brain is participating even when your body isn't.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Some truths are embodied, not spoken. Dance teaches that the body knows things the mind cannot articulate. Movement expresses what language fails to reach.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 157. Tomorrow, we'll explore pretending on purpose—theater and acting. Until then, move to music—your body knows how.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Movement Expression - Let Your Body Speak
growTrack.learning_objective: Use movement to access and express emotion
growTrack.activity: Put on music and move—in private if you're shy. Don't perform; just let your body respond to rhythm. Notice how movement affects your mood. Your body has wisdom that sitting still can't access.
